correctness.rationale: The exact 2x2 Schur complement q_p(r) has logarithmic derivative (2-p)(r^p-1)/[(1+r^p)(1+(p-1)r^p)], yielding the sharp minimum at r=1 for 1<p<2. Global squared-defect convexity follows by matched C1 boundary derivatives; squared convexity plus 2-homogeneity implies a norm. Absolute-norm monotonicity lifts sufficiency to arbitrary Banach Y, while restriction to a unit vector in Y proves necessity. Explicit endpoint failures and the p=2 identity cover every remaining case; a finite stdlib stress checker supplements, not substitutes for, the proof.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison shows that arXiv:2407.15112 provides the norm/dilation criterion and p-dependent counterexamples, not the exact scalar-coordinate threshold, while arXiv:1405.0431 provides the global p-1 convexity constant but not the strictly larger coordinate-specific threshold 2^(2/p)(p-1)/p. Targeted semantic and public literature searches found no equivalent conclusion; an unindexed equivalent remains possible.
residual_risks: An equivalent scalar-defect convexity threshold could exist under a different name in less indexed Banach renorming or interpolation literature.

value.rationale: A complete iff classification across all p∈[1,∞] and all nonzero real or complex Banach summands, with an exact nontrivial sharp coefficient c_p and an abrupt phase distinction at p=2. It identifies the admissible isometric-dilation regime for a natural rank-one family not directly resolved by the motivating qualitative theorem; p-1 curvature bounds do not give its optimal threshold.
